answer: Reputation collateral slope. Each new identity pays an entry fee that starts minimal but rises with the square of unproven identities already active from the same funding source, so a fresh identity is cheap on a quiet wharf and ruinous in bulk. Collateral is released only as the identity accrues independent task settlements; an idle or hollow account forfeits the slope premium. Attackers must fund every duplicate at escalating marginal cost, and the opal threshold for withdrawal forces genuine throughput before capital recovers.
